source_text: Ac per hoc bardissime argumentatus es, quod si apostolus Paulus per imitationem transisse peccatum voluisset intellegi, diabolum magis quam Adam nominasset; cum clareat, et hominis et diaboli malum non nisi imitatione transire potuisse. Verum disiecto quod tu exstruxeras, non tam meis quam ipsius rationis manibus, quid nunc a nobis afferatur attende.
pass_a_gloss: And through this you have argued most dully, that if the apostle Paul had wanted it to be understood that sin passed through imitation, he would have named the devil rather than Adam; when it is clear that the evil both of a human being and of the devil could have passed only by imitation. But, what you had built having been thrown apart, not so much by my hands as by those of reason itself, attend to what is now brought by us.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Your argument, then, was exceedingly stupid: that if the apostle Paul had wanted sin’s passage to be understood as imitation, he would have named the devil rather than Adam. For it is clear that the evil of either a human being or the devil could pass on only through imitation. But now that your construction has been torn apart, not so much by my hands as by those of reason itself, attend to what we bring forward (compare Romans 5:12).

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
